about: Stages and timing for the peak-event playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: plan
stages.do: Rank the campaigns to run around the event, with send windows, audiences and clashes on the calendar.

stages.name: collections
stages.do: Define the event's landing collections, one topic at a time, for the user to set up in the dashboard. Skip it when the landing pages exist and work.

stages.name: readiness
stages.do: Check data, merchandising, search, marketing and on-site readiness for the event window; blockers first.

stages.name: vouchers
stages.do: Check every voucher pool will last through the event's planned sends. Record no_vouchers when the event uses none.

stages.name: preflight
stages.do: Check every send scheduled in the event window: GO, GO WITH CAUTION or NO-GO, with what to fix.

stages.name: collisions
stages.do: Check the event window's sends for overlapping audiences, busy days, email and SMS on the same day, and missing frequency caps.

stages.name: review
stages.do: After the event, compare the event period with the period before it and explain what moved revenue.

notes.send_checks_days_before_event: Days before the event starts when the preflight (and so the collisions) stage becomes due: sends are scheduled by then, and there's still time to fix them. The assistant records it with stage --name preflight --not-before at the start of the run, from the event start date the user gives.
notes.review_after_event_days: Days after the event ends before the review stage is due. Discovery reporting runs about 2 days behind, and the explainer needs the whole event period. The assistant records it with stage --name review --not-before at the start of the run, from the event end date the user gives.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet: the review found the event's last days not yet in the reports. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, which product it needs in a run on both (product), what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when. This playbook has no not_before: its waits are keyed on the event dates the user gives, recorded with stage --not-before. A run with only one product gets the other product's stages offered for skipping.
